description: A melody generated as a walk through a scale: a seeded skeleton that repeats exactly, with a chance at each step of straying to a neighbouring note

params.text: Picks the scale the walk moves through, from the shared list of nineteen
Sets the root the scale is built on, C through B
Sets the first step of the window that is played, 1 to 8
Sets the last step of the window that is played, 1 to 8; setting it before the start plays the window backwards
Leans the walk upward or downward; at the centre it is as likely to rise as to fall
Sets how large each move is, from steps of a second at one end of the travel to leaps of up to an octave at the other
Sets the chance of straying from the skeleton at each step; at none the skeleton plays unchanged, and a stray does not shift the notes after it
Sets the chance that an odd-numbered step of the walk is silent
Sets the chance that an even-numbered step of the walk is silent
Sets the chance that a step jumps an octave up or down
Sets the chance that a step retriggers as two or three short bursts, keeping its own pitch
Rolls a fresh skeleton for the playing pattern on each press
Returns to the first active pattern on each press
Picks the second voice's interval: Off, a third, a fifth or an octave up or down, or Varied, which draws a consonant interval per step, some of them moving the other way

inputs.text: Each rise advances the walk by one step; the module has no clock of its own
A rise returns to the first active pattern
A rise rolls a fresh skeleton for the playing pattern
Sets the root, a volt per octave snapped to semitones, added to the root knob
Leans the walk up or down, added to the gravity knob at a tenth per volt
Changes the move size, added to the drift knob at a tenth per volt
Changes the chance of straying, added to the branch knob at a tenth per volt
Picks the scale, one volt per scale, added to the scale knob; it takes the same signal another module's scale output sends
Changes the chance of an odd step being silent, added to that knob at a tenth per volt
Changes the chance of an even step being silent, added to that knob at a tenth per volt
Changes the chance of an octave jump, added to that knob at a tenth per volt
Changes the chance of a burst, added to the ratchet knob at a tenth per volt
Moves the first step of the played window, one volt per step, added to the start knob
Moves the last step of the played window, one volt per step, added to the end knob

outputs.text: The melody as a volt per octave, quantized to the root and scale
The melody's gate, of the length set on the menu
The second voice as a volt per octave, at the interval the harmony switch names

notes: the walk moves only on an external clock; the module has no tempo of its own
the eight patterns, their repeat counts, whether each is active, and the per-step gates are all edited on the display, which cannot be reached by clicking for help
a step switched off on the display is a forced rest whatever the rest knobs say, which is the usual reason for an unexpected gap
the next note is drawn from hand-written tables of what follows what in that scale rather than at random, so a seven-note scale pulls toward chord tones and resolves its leading note
menu: Pattern cell: click = edit · dbl-click = on/off · boxes = repeats · R = reseed — a label saying what the mouse does on a pattern slot
Gate row (focused pattern): click = on/off · shift-click = tie — a label saying what the mouse does on the step gates
Gate length — a slider setting how much of each step the gate output holds high
Glide — a slider setting how far the pitch output slides between notes
Start each cycle on root — grounds the first step of every cycle on the tonic
Vary shaping each run (rests/holds/octaves/ratchets) — rolls fresh rests, octave jumps and bursts on every pass rather than keeping them fixed to the pattern
Walk range — a label over the two range choices below it
±1 octave — holds the walk inside one octave either side of where it started
±2 octaves — lets the walk reach two octaves either side of where it started
New core for current pattern — rolls a fresh skeleton for the pattern being edited
New cores for all patterns — rolls fresh skeletons for all eight patterns
